subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Alfred Peet: Godfather of American Specialty Coffee
description: A quick win: understand Alfred Peet: Godfather of American Specialty Coffee.

hook.text: Dutch immigrant Alfred Peet opened Peet's Coffee in Berkeley, California in 1966—and changed how Americans tasted coffee.

buildup.text: Peet grew up in his father's coffee trade in the Netherlands. He was appalled by the weak, stale coffee Americans drank.

discovery.text: Peet roasted small batches of high-quality beans dark and fresh. Customers tasted the difference immediately—it was a revelation.

twist.text: Three early customers—Baldwin, Siegl, and Bowker—founded Starbucks in 1971 using Peet's roasting methods.

climax.text: Without Peet, there's no Starbucks, no specialty movement, no third wave. He lit the match; America's coffee revolution followed.

punchline.text: One immigrant, one small shop, one higher standard. American coffee was reborn.

quiz.question: How did Alfred Peet influence Starbucks?
options: Three of his customers founded Starbucks using his methods and standards
